title: You clicked a suspicious link — question explanation
learningObjective: Report suspected phishing or accidental interaction promptly through the approved channel
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: You clicked a suspicious link and entered your work password before realizing the page was fake.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Report suspected phishing or accidental interaction promptly through the approved channel
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option D: Report immediately through the approved security channel and follow instructions to secure the account from a trusted device. Prompt reporting enables the organization to contain possible credential compromise and assess impact.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Public posting may expose organizational details and does not trigger incident response. Option B: Non-reporting delays containment and may allow the account to be misused. Option C: Waiting can give an attacker more time to use exposed credentials.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Contact the security/helpdesk team immediately. From a trusted device, follow their direction to reset credentials, revoke sessions and inspect account activity. Fast, accurate reporting helps limit harm; do not hide accidental interaction.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Fast, accurate reporting helps limit harm; do not hide accidental interaction.

narration: Scenario: You clicked a suspicious link and entered your work password before realizing the page was fake. Safest response: Option D: Report immediately through the approved security channel and follow instructions to secure the account from a trusted device. Prompt reporting enables the organization to contain possible credential compromise and assess impact. Option A is unsafe because Public posting may expose organizational details and does not trigger incident response. Option B is unsafe because Non-reporting delays containment and may allow the account to be misused. Option C is unsafe because Waiting can give an attacker more time to use exposed credentials. In practice: Contact the security/helpdesk team immediately. From a trusted device, follow their direction to reset credentials, revoke sessions and inspect account activity. Key takeaway: Fast, accurate reporting helps limit harm; do not hide accidental interaction.

generationInstructions: Use the narration as the voiceover source; preserve its meaning and do not add unsupported technical claims.

Human-review the rendered video for factual accuracy, spelling, pronunciation, captions and timing before marking it validated.
accessibility: Separate synchronized captions and transcript required. Written explanation is the fallback. Avoid flashing and color-only information. Provide a static equivalent of all essential 3D visuals.
